subject: Onboarding kickoff: model vetting, context needs & token scan
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia@novasync.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Lee <tom.lee@novasync.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Onboarding kickoff — model/context & token snapshot

Hi Marcus —

Thanks for the quick intro call earlier. Per our discussion, I wanted to share our initial stats so your CS/implementation team can start thinking about model fit and sizing. Attaching a small CSV with a 30‑day token sample (novasync_token_report.csv) and a short list of prompt examples (MVP_prompt_examples.md). Quick highlights: 

- Monthly active users (MAU): ~45,000
- Monthly tokens (30-day window): ~3.1M tokens total (includes prompts + responses)
- Typical interaction: prompt ~200–350 tokens, generated response ~250–500 tokens
- Long‑context workflows: ~15% of requests are multi‑document summarizations, require up to 16k context; those are mostly asynchronous and can tolerate slightly higher latency
- Peak concurrency: observed bursts up to ~35 reqs/s during our morning rush (PST)

Important constraints: all customer data stays in our VPC until the first week of August; after that we will consider a hosted pilot. We care about latency for interactive flows (<400ms tail for short prompts) and unit cost for the high-volume short Q&A path.

Can your team propose an initial shortlist of candidate models (and variants) and a rough token/instance sizing for Dedicated or hosted routes? Also please flag any immediate red flags for the 16k workflows.

Thanks —
Alicia
Director, Product
Novasync

Alicia — thanks for the data and examples, super helpful. Looping in Grace (CS lead) and Priyom (runtime/modeling) to propose a concrete shortlist and sizing. Initial answers below, will follow with a short writeup: 

1) Quick red flags:
   - 16k context summarizations are doable but will affect unit economics; we typically recommend using a specialized longer‑context variant only for the async summarization path with separate routing.
   - 35 reqs/s peak with 45k MAU and ~3M monthly tokens implies high QPS bursts — we should design for autoscale headroom and prefix/KV caching for repeated user context.

2) What we’ll deliver in the next message:
   - 3 candidate model variants (low-cost high-throughput, balanced, high-quality long-context)
   - Token-per-second and GPU-instance sizing for both hosted and Dedicated options
   - Batching & caching suggestions to meet the <400ms tail for short prompts

I’ve attached an SOW draft we typically use; we’ll adapt after we confirm traffic slices.

Best,
Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Marcus / team —

Quick clarifications to help with sizing:

- Token distribution: ~82% of requests are short Q&A (prompt < 300 tokens, expected response < 350 tokens). 
- ~8% are multi-turn chat threads where user history (avg 6 messages) is relevant — average expanded context for that path is ~1.5k tokens.
- ~10% are large document ops (summaries and extractive QA) that need a full context window up to 16k tokens; these jobs are launched asynchronously from the client and can be queued.
- We expect growth: plan for 2x tokens in 6 months if retention/feature usage ramps per our roadmap.
- Compliance: we need SOC2 evidence and a brief on data retention policies before enabling hosted pilot.

Also — latency SLA for interactive flows: target 95th < 400ms for the short Q&A path (we understand this is tight). For the long context jobs, 95th < 10s is acceptable.

Let us know if you'd like raw logs or a sample QPS timeline from the last 7 days.

— Alicia

Hi Alicia — great detail, thanks. Priyom and I mapped your traffic to three candidate deployment profiles and model variants. High-level recommendations below; we can turn these into an itemized sizing table for Dedicated vs Hosted in the next update.

Candidate model slate (by workload slice):
1) Short Q&A (82% of traffic) — high throughput / low latency, focus on cost
   - Candidate: Redwood-Lite-13B (8k) quantized (int8) or Llama-2-13B-chat int8
   - Rationale: good cost/token, can be served with aggressive batching and 1–2 GPU instances for baseline; use continuous batching + 50ms lookahead to keep tail low.

2) Multi‑turn chat (8%) — medium context, conversational quality
   - Candidate: Llama-2-70B-chat-16k (q4f16 / mixed precision) or Red-13B-retrieval-enhanced
   - Rationale: better multi-turn consistency, keep smaller KV cache per-session, route by user history length.

3) Long document summarization (10%) — up to 16k context, asynchronous
   - Candidate: OpenLong-34B-16k (fp16) or a 70B long-context variant on Dedicated nodes
   - Rationale: serving a 16k window is memory-heavy; run these on Dedicated capacity or isolated hosted long-context nodes and queue jobs to optimize GPU utilization.

Sizing & ops notes (quick):
- Baseline hosted path for short Q&A: assume ~5–8 vGPUs (A100x) for 35 req/s peak if you want <400ms 95th with batching and prefix caching; Dedicated sizing will be ~3–5 reserved GPUs with autoscale for bursts depending on batch sizes.
- For the 16k async path: schedule ~1–2 Dedicated 80GB GPUs for peak batch processing; because jobs are asynchronous we can schedule them on off‑peak windows to amortize cost.
- Caching: enable prefix/KV cache for repeat queries and session affinity to reduce compute by ~15–25% on short Q&A.
- Rollout: start hosted pilot for short Q&A with the Lite variant, then enable Dedicated long‑context nodes for the summarization workload.

Security/compliance: Marcus / Monica — can you share our SOC2 checklist and a short note on data residency? Alicia, we can redact logs and run a brief pen‑test questionnaire before hosted pilot.

Next steps:
- Marcus to send a side‑by‑side Dedicated vs Hosted cost and GPU count (by model slice).
- Grace to produce a 2‑page runbook for routing policies (short vs medium vs long).
- Alicia to confirm pilot start date and whether Novasync will provide 7‑day QPS logs.

Thanks —
Grace
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Alicia / Tom —

Thanks for the confirmation and the clarifications. Attached is a short snapshot we prepared (SOW_draft_v2.pdf) and a proposed minimal pilot plan:

1) Pilot scope (4 weeks):
   - Traffic: short Q&A path only (~82%): Redwood‑Lite‑13B int8 hosted pilot; limit to 25% of live traffic to start.
   - Observability: enable per-route token & latency dashboards; Redwood will provide daily token burn reports.
   - Long context: hold summarization jobs on Dedicated queue (no live user routing) until SOC2 signoff.

2) Proposed sizing (hosted pilot, initial):
   - Redwood‑Lite‑13B int8: 2 reserved vGPUs with autoscale up to 6 for peak (expected to cover <400ms 95th for short prompts with batching tuned).
   - If you prefer Dedicated for cost predictability, equivalent would be 3–4 reserved 80GB instances with burst policy.

3) Deliverables & timeline:
   - Day 0: Intent to pilot + sample logs delivered by Novasync.
   - Day 3–5: Model tuning & batching config; test run on 10% traffic.
   - Week 2: Expand to 25% traffic; collect SLA telemetry.
   - Week 4: Review & decide next steps (Dedicated vs full-hosted roll).

4) Security/compliance ask (required before long‑context live routing):
   - Novasync to sign SOC2 NDA addendum and provide a point of contact for the audit evidence.

Please let us know if the pilot scope works; we can convert the SOW draft to a short pilot addendum after you confirm.

Best,
Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
